original_target.title: Stationary theta networks on Riemannian two-spheres

full_original_statement:
Let $`g`$ be any smooth Riemannian metric on $`S^2`$. Must there exist two distinct points $`p,q\in S^2`$, positive lengths $`L_1,L_2,L_3`$, and three embedded unit-speed geodesic arcs

```math
\gamma_i:[0,L_i]\longrightarrow(S^2,g),\qquad
\gamma_i(0)=p,\quad\gamma_i(L_i)=q,
```

whose interiors are pairwise disjoint and satisfy

```math
\sum_{i=1}^3\dot\gamma_i(0)=0,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^3\bigl(-\dot\gamma_i(L_i)\bigr)=0?
```

Thus the union is an embedded graph homeomorphic to the Greek letter $`\Theta`$, with three edges and two triple junctions. The outgoing unit tangents at each junction meet at angles $`2\pi/3`$. The arcs need not minimize distance globally between $`p`$ and $`q`$. Their lengths must remain positive and the two vertices distinct.

sources.scope_comparison: The actual existence and multiplicity theorem assumes the sphere metric is sufficiently C2-close to the round metric. The introduction explicitly retains theta-network existence for arbitrary positively curved spheres, hence also the target with every smooth metric. A stationary graph of unspecified topology, eyeglasses/figure-eight alternatives, density for generic metrics, or singular doubled-polygon examples do not force three positive embedded edges and two distinct balanced junctions for every smooth g. No full matching claim found.
